lesson.title: Ischioanal fossa, pudendal canal and anal region
lesson.summary: The ischioanal fossa contains fat that permits expansion of the anal canal.
tags: Ischioanal fossa, pudendal canal and anal region
lesson.section: 31. Ischioanal Fossa; 34. Pudendal Canal and Internal Pudendal Pathway; 35. Rectum and Anal Canal

steps.title: Ischioanal Fossa
steps.body:
The ischioanal fossa is a fat-filled wedge-shaped space in the anal triangle. It allows expansion of the anal canal and transmits inferior rectal vessels and nerves. Its lateral wall includes obturator internus fascia with pudendal canal.

Medial wall: external anal sphincter and levator ani/pelvic diaphragm. Lateral wall: obturator internus muscle and fascia. Posterior boundary: sacrotuberous ligament and gluteus maximus region. Anterior recess extends into urogenital triangle above perineal membrane region. Contents: fat, inferior rectal nerve/vessels, lymphatics.

steps.title: Pudendal Canal and Internal Pudendal Pathway
steps.body:
The pudendal canal is a fascial tunnel in the obturator internus fascia on the lateral wall of the ischioanal fossa. It contains pudendal nerve and internal pudendal vessels, which supply the perineum and external genitalia.

Pudendal nerve roots: S2-S4. Route: greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, around ischial spine/sacrospinous ligament, lesser sciatic foramen, pudendal canal. Branches: inferior rectal nerve, perineal nerve, dorsal nerve of penis or clitoris. Internal pudendal artery follows the same route and gives inferior rectal, perineal, and dorsal/deep arteries of erectile tissues.

steps.title: Rectum and Anal Canal
steps.body:
The rectum is the terminal pelvic part of the large intestine, beginning at S3 and ending at the anorectal junction. It is related posteriorly to sacrum/coccyx and anteriorly to bladder/prostate/seminal vesicles in male or vagina/uterus region in female. The anal canal passes through the pelvic floor and perineum.

Rectum upper third is peritoneal anteriorly and laterally; middle third anteriorly; lower third is infraperitoneal. Arteries: superior rectal from IMA, middle rectal from internal iliac, inferior rectal from internal pudendal. Venous drainage forms portal-systemic communication: superior rectal to portal system; middle/inferior rectal to caval system. Upper anal canal lymph drains to internal iliac nodes; lower anal canal lymph drains to superficial inguinal nodes. Internal anal sphincter is smooth muscle; external anal sphincter is skeletal muscle.

steps.title: Why does the ischioanal fossa contain fat rather than a rigid muscular wall around the anal canal?
steps.body: Fat-filled space allows the anal canal to expand during passage while preserving room for nearby neurovascular branches. The fossa's boundaries provide support without constraining the canal as a solid ring. Inferior rectal nerves and vessels cross the space from lateral routes toward the sphincter and skin. The two fossae can communicate posteriorly through related spaces, so regional processes may extend across the midline. A coronal view reveals this relationship more clearly than a simple inferior surface outline.

steps.title: Apply the anatomy and resolve a common confusion
steps.body: The ischioanal fossa contains fat that permits expansion of the anal canal. Its medial boundary includes levator ani and the external sphincter; laterally lie obturator internus and its fascia. Inferior rectal branches cross the fat toward the anal region, whereas the main pudendal bundle travels in the lateral fascial canal. Distinguish the smooth internal sphincter from the skeletal external sphincter, and the pectinate mucosal line from the pelvic-floor boundary.
